## The problem it solves

The `AD` field in VCF/GATK-exported tables is a comma-separated string (`ref,alt`). Fast readers guess column types per file, so the same field arrives as character in one file and numeric in another, and the alternate-allele count is silently lost or shifted. Downstream allele-frequency tests then run on the wrong numbers with no error.

## Approach

- Read AD columns as character explicitly, then split on the comma. Never rely on the reader's type inference for these fields.
- Return reference and alternate depths as integer columns with a per-site total-depth check (`ref + alt == DP` where DP is available; mismatches are flagged, not dropped).
- Allele-frequency comparison between pools that accounts for two sources of variance: binomial sampling of reads and the finite number of individuals in the pool. Point estimates alone overstate confidence for small pools.
- Command-line entry point through a Snakemake workflow so the same parsing and tests run unchanged on the cluster.

## QC defaults carried from prior work

| Parameter | Default | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Genotype quality | GQ ≥ 90 | Standard used across the lab's pool-seq calls |
| Minimum depth | Site-level, set per dataset | Must be chosen from the depth distribution of the data, not fixed |

: {.project-meta}

## Status

Package structure, tests, and documentation exist; the public release is pending a final review of the example data shipped with the package.
